record.summary: Non-binding framework for the responsible use of AI across the New Zealand Public Service. It sets a vision, 5 principles informed by the OECD AI Principles (inclusive and sustainable development, human-centred values, transparency and explainability, safety and security, and accountability), the legal and policy context, and 6 pillars of the Government Chief Digital Officer's AI work programme: governance, guardrails, capability, innovation, social licence and global voice. It asks agencies to disclose when they use AI systems and to provide human oversight throughout the AI lifecycle.
record.notes: The framework sits within New Zealand's National AI Strategy, launched in July 2025. It follows Cabinet's decision of June 2024 to promote the OECD AI principles, and it records Cabinet's light-touch, proportionate and risk-based approach to AI regulation, under which further intervention should use existing mechanisms in preference to a standalone AI Act. The page shows 'Last updated 29 January 2025' although it refers to the strategy launched in July 2025.

summary.locator: Overview of the Public Service AI Framework
summary.quote: sets a vision for AI in New Zealand’s Public Service defines 5 key principles to guide Public Service AI use outlines the policy context for Public Service AI use outlines 6 key pillars
We use the OECD’s values-based AI principles to inform the principles of the Public Service AI Framework.
Inclusive, sustainable development Public Service AI systems should contribute to inclusive growth and sustainable development
Agencies need to provide human oversight throughout the AI lifecycle to ensure ethical and appropriate use.
To support this, agencies should publicly disclose: when AI systems are used
Governance — to support transparency and human accountability in Public Service AI use.
Global voice — to ensure international counterparts see New Zealand as a trusted AI partner.
Human-centred values • Privacy and data ethics • Upholding democracy and the rule of law • Human and labour rights • Human oversight
Guardrails Support safe and trustworthy use of AI and its underpinning data
